question: payment

request.from: a cloud container in a datacenter network, one IP, user agent curl/8
request.body: the same priced route requested three times at 06:06:08Z, 06:06:11Z and 06:06:14Z, three seconds apart, with nothing else changed between them

headers.payment-required: base64 of the x402 document; it decodes to the JSON body the values below are read from

decoded.amount: 2000 units of USDC on each of the four entries, unchanged from the 2026-09-28 reading
decoded.payTo-stable: all three responses carry the same recipients: 0x480CD46E6faDe651a0437DeaddA53D5c8e7D846A on Base (eip155:8453), Arbitrum (eip155:42161) and Polygon (eip155:137), and 5yASLjtNssGXDv6bR9e71WXKxRymDiUzbgkGPqkQNgRn on Solana (solana:5eykt4UsFv8P8NJdTREpY1vzqKqZKvdp). Nothing rotates between requests on this surface today
decoded.feePayer: the Solana entry's extra.feePayer is BENrLoUbndxoNMUS5JXApGMtNykLjFXXixMtpDwDR9SP in all three responses, the only field in that entry's extra, where the three EVM entries carry name and version
decoded.same-address-at-an-unrelated-vendor: agents.allium.so, a different vendor with a different product, presented the same address as its own Solana extra.feePayer in three responses read between 06:05:02Z and 06:06:07Z, the minute before these. Allium's own Solana payTo rotated in each of those three responses while this fee payer did not (probe record p-20260929-allium-machine-payments-unpaid). One address standing in the fee-payer slot of two unrelated vendors' challenges places it in settlement infrastructure the two share rather than at either vendor. What that infrastructure is was not established: no page read by this reporter names it
decoded.bearing-on-the-2026-09-21-records: nine records filed here on 2026-09-21 name BENrLoUb... as this surface's Solana payTo, and the 2026-09-28 and 2026-09-29 readings both read 5yASLjtNss... there. This measurement does not settle which is right, because two readings a week apart cannot rule out a vendor changing the address. It removes one innocent explanation and weakens another: the recipient is not per-request on this surface, so the difference is not rotation between calls; and an address that an unrelated vendor presents as a fee payer is a poor candidate for this vendor's recipient. The 2026-09-21 pass archived no bytes, so what it read cannot be re-read

finding: Three unpaid requests to one priced Bitrefill route, three seconds apart on 2026-09-29, returned identical recipients: one EVM address on Base, Arbitrum and Polygon and one Solana address, with the Solana entry's extra.feePayer the same in all three. This surface does not mint a recipient per request. In the minute before, an unrelated vendor's priced endpoint (agents.allium.so) presented the same Solana fee payer while rotating its own Solana recipient on every request, so that address belongs to settlement infrastructure the two vendors share rather than to either of them. This is filed against the open disagreement in the Bitrefill entry, where this registry's 2026-09-21 records name that fee payer as this surface's payTo: it does not settle it, since a vendor may change a recipient in a week and the 2026-09-21 pass archived no bytes to re-read, but it removes per-request rotation as an explanation and makes the address an implausible recipient for this vendor. No payment was made; one IP is one sample.

reproducibility.command: for i in 1 2 3; do curl -s 'https://api.bitrefill.com/x402/gift-cards/search?query=amazon' | python3 -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); [print(a['network'], a['payTo'], (a.get('extra') or {}).get('feePayer')) for a in d['accepts']]"; sleep 3; done
